answers.label: Q.1
answers.finalAnswer: crossing one threshold (difficulty) after another; by steady effort and practice until the hard task becomes easy; not complain, accept the challenge and determine to cross it; steering clear of thresholds and staying in a rut; one can learn and begin new things at any age; never rest but keep aiming at ever higher goals; made a success of it; by continuing to cross thresholds (taking up new challenges); A careful driver steers clear of crowded roads at rush hour; rut
answers.solution:
(a) Progress in life depends a good deal on crossing one threshold (difficulty) after another.

(b) We can accomplish the most difficult tasks by steady effort and practice. Like the little nephew, who found writing his name very hard work at first but now writes it with ease, what is difficult today becomes easy if we keep trying.

(c) When a new difficulty obstructs our path, we should not complain. We should accept the challenge and determine to cross it, just as we have crossed many thresholds in the past.

(d) Real progress stops when people steer clear of thresholds: they avoid anything that needs genuine thinking and energy, stay in a rut, and make no effort to seek out new obstacles to overcome.

(e) De Morgan's life teaches that it is never too late to begin something new. He started writing novels after he was sixty, which shows that a person can go on learning throughout life.

(f) It means that we should never rest content with what we have achieved, but should keep setting ourselves higher and nobler goals and keep working towards them.

(g) He made a success of his new business.

(h) Middle aged and elderly people add brilliance to their lives by continuing to cross thresholds, that is, by taking up new challenges such as a new business or a new kind of work, and by going on learning.

(j) A careful driver steers clear of crowded roads at rush hour. ('Steer clear of' means to avoid.)

(k) rut (a fixed habit or dull way of doing things; 'They prefer to stay in a rut').

answers.label: Q.2(a)
answers.solution: A suitable title is 'A Morning Through the Window'. The poem describes the simple, joyful sights a man sees from his window one morning: a butterfly in his garden and two laughing girls on the sidewalk.

answers.label: Q.2(b)
answers.finalAnswer: Simile: Waved in the air like Tunisian silk; Personification: a laughing sidewalk
answers.solution:
1. Simile: 'Waved in the air like Tunisian silk'. The cadence of the girls' laughter is compared to silk waving in the air, using 'like'.

2. Personification: 'a laughing sidewalk'. The sidewalk is given a human quality, laughter, because the laughing girls walk on it.

(Other devices in the poem: alliteration in 'red and radiant', and inversion in 'A turquoise skirt wore the one'.)

answers.label: Q.2(c)
answers.finalAnswer: Simple everyday sights seen from a window, a butterfly and two laughing girls, can fill an ordinary morning with joy, more than grand scenes on a screen.
answers.solution: The poem shows that happiness lies in the simple sights of everyday life. One morning a man opens his curtains and sees a bright orange butterfly in his sunny garden and two cheerful girls walking and laughing on the sidewalk. He does not need grand scenes of harvests or mountains on a screen; these small, natural moments of beauty and joy are enough to brighten his day.

answers.label: Q.2(d)
answers.finalAnswer: The laughter of the two maidens is compared to Tunisian silk waving in the air.
answers.solution:
As printed the question says 'smile', a word that does not occur in the poem; it is a misprint for 'simile'.

The simile is used in the line 'Waved in the air like Tunisian silk'. The soft, flowing sound (cadence) of the two maidens' laughter is compared to fine Tunisian silk waving in the air, to show how light and pleasant their laughter was.

answers.label: Q.2(e)
answers.finalAnswer: One wore a turquoise skirt, the other a chocolate T-shirt.
answers.solution: One of the maidens wore a turquoise skirt and the other wore a chocolate T-shirt ('A turquoise skirt wore the one, / A Chocolate T-Shirt the other').

answers.label: Q.2(f)
answers.solution:
(i) Rhythm: cadence ('As the cadence of their laughter')

(ii) Walked confidently: strutted ('Strutted two maidens together')

answers.label: Q.3
answers.solution:
Topics attempted: (a), (b) and (c).

(a) Adversity Brings Out the Best in Man

Adversity means hard times such as illness, poverty, failure or danger. Nobody likes difficult days, yet they often bring out the best in us. When life is easy, we never discover how strong we really are. When trouble comes, we are forced to think, to work harder and to find new ways to succeed.

History is full of such examples. Abraham Lincoln lost many elections before he became President of America. Helen Keller could neither see nor hear, yet she became a famous writer. Our soldiers show their greatest courage in the face of danger.

Adversity also teaches us patience, courage and sympathy for others who suffer. Gold shines brightest after it passes through fire. So we should not fear hard times. We should face them bravely, because they make us stronger and better people.

(b) The Value of Friendship

A friend is a person who loves us, trusts us and stands by us in good times and bad. Friendship is one of the most precious gifts of life. A true friend doubles our joys and halves our sorrows.

A good friend gives us honest advice. He tells us when we are wrong and helps us correct our mistakes. In times of trouble, when others leave us, a true friend stays by our side. That is why it is said, 'A friend in need is a friend indeed.'

However, we must choose our friends carefully. Bad company can lead us astray, while good friends help us grow. We too must be loyal, honest and caring towards our friends, because a friendship lasts only when both people value it and look after it.

(c) The Role of Students in Bringing About a Welcome Change in Our Environment

Our environment is in danger. The air and water are polluted, forests are being cut down and plastic is everywhere. Students can play a big part in changing this, because they are young, energetic and full of new ideas.

Students can begin with their own habits. They can switch off lights and fans when they are not needed, save water and carry cloth bags instead of plastic ones. They can plant trees in their schools and colonies and look after them.

Students can also spread awareness. Through posters, plays, rallies and eco-clubs, they can persuade their families and neighbours to keep their surroundings clean. If every student does a little, together they can make a big difference, and a clean, green earth will be their gift to the future.

answers.label: Q.4
answers.solution:
Rahul's Presence of Mind

Rahul was alone at home. Suddenly the phone rang. He picked it up and a polite voice said, 'Hello, I am calling from the bank. Your father's ATM card has been blocked. Tell me the number that has just come on his phone, or all his money will be lost.'

Rahul's father had gone to the office and had left his old mobile at home. Just then a message with a six-digit code flashed on it. Rahul felt nervous. The man kept saying, 'Hurry up, son! There is very little time.'

Then Rahul remembered his father's words: 'A bank never asks for a secret code on the phone.' He said firmly, 'I will not give you any number. My father will visit the bank himself,' and he put the phone down.

He at once rang up his father and told him everything. His father informed the bank and the cyber police. A few days later, the police caught a gang that had cheated many people in the town in the same way.

That evening his father patted Rahul on the back and said, 'Your presence of mind has saved our hard-earned money.' Rahul felt very proud of himself.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
12, Rajpur Road
Dehradun

15 June 2019

The Station House Officer
Rajpur Police Station
Dehradun

Subject: Complaint against the use of loudspeakers in our locality

Sir,

I wish to draw your attention to the nuisance caused by loudspeakers in our locality, Rajpur Road. Although the government has banned their use, people here continue to play them loudly at weddings, parties and functions, often till late at night.

My examinations begin next week and I am unable to concentrate on my studies because of the constant noise. Many other students of the area face the same problem. The noise also disturbs old people, patients and small children, who cannot rest or sleep properly.

I therefore request you to take strict action against those who break the law and to ensure that loudspeakers are not used in our area. Regular checking by the police would help to solve this problem.

Thanking you,

Yours faithfully,
Amit Kumar

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
Title: The Noble Teacher

Teaching is the noblest profession because the teacher shapes the character of children. Besides training their minds, he teaches them good citizenship, cleanliness, polite speech and good manners. Such habits are hard to form, and only a teacher who himself lives a simple, pure and disciplined life can develop them in his pupils. Moreover, his constant company with the young keeps him youthful and cheerful and helps him forget his personal worries.

(72 words)

answers.label: Q.7
answers.finalAnswer: He said that he need not go.; He speaks as if he were an educated person.; Nobody informed me that he had left yesterday.; Borrowing is not as good as lending.; I will always remember you all my life.
answers.solution:
(a) He said that he need not go. ('Need not' does not change its form in indirect speech; 'He said that he did not need to go' is also correct.)

(b) He speaks as if he were an educated person. ('As if' is followed by 'were' for an unreal situation.)

(c) Nobody informed me that he had left yesterday.

(d) Borrowing is not as good as lending. (The comparative 'better than' becomes the positive 'not as good as', with the two things changing places.)

(e) I will always remember you all my life. ('Never forget' becomes 'always remember'.)

answers.finalAnswer: (ii) ignore the past; (iii) Invite someone to fight; (iii) Done in an instant; (ii) in the midst of successes; (ii) a man of no substance
answers.solution:
(a) (ii) ignore the past. To let bygones be bygones is to forget past quarrels.

(b) (iii) Invite someone to fight. To throw down the gauntlet is to issue a challenge.

(c) (iii) Done in an instant. 'At the drop of a hat' means immediately, without any hesitation.

(d) (ii) in the midst of successes. 'On a roll' means enjoying a run of successes.

answers.label: Q.12
answers.finalAnswer: (ii) fallen out; (i) pulled up; (ii) cheered on; (iii) look up; (iii) threw up
answers.solution:
(a) (ii) fallen out: to fall out is to quarrel.
(b) (i) pulled up: to pull up is to scold someone for a fault.
(c) (ii) cheered on: to cheer on is to encourage by shouting.
(d) (iii) look up: to look up a word is to search for it in a dictionary.
(e) (iii) threw up: to throw up is to vomit ('green about the gills' means looking sick).

answers.label: Q.13
answers.finalAnswer: Hardly had we walked one kilometre when they stopped us.; The memory is too vivid for me ever to forget.; All we cared about was food and sleep.; Herbert did not accept the job offer without consulting his parents.; Put your tools away lest the children should fall over them.
answers.solution:
(a) Hardly had we walked one kilometre when they stopped us. (After 'Hardly' the helping verb comes before the subject.)

(b) The memory is too vivid for me ever to forget.

(c) All we cared about was food and sleep.

(d) Herbert did not accept the job offer without consulting his parents.

(e) Put your tools away lest the children should fall over them. ('Lest' is followed by 'should', never by 'not'.)

answers.label: Q.14
answers.finalAnswer: One of the reasons for his failure is his careless attitude.; He need not go there.; Delhi Capitals would have won IPL 2019 if they had played well.; The number of people we need to hire is thirteen.; If you freeze water, it becomes a solid.
answers.solution:
(a) One of the reasons for his failure is his careless attitude. ('One of' takes a plural noun, and we say 'reason for'.)

(b) He need not go there. (When 'need' is a modal it takes no 's' and no 'to'. 'He does not need to go there' is also correct.)

(c) Delhi Capitals would have won IPL 2019 if they had played well. (The 'if' clause takes the past perfect, not 'would have'.)

(d) The number of people we need to hire is thirteen. ('The number' is singular and takes 'is'.)

(e) If you freeze water, it becomes a solid. (A scientific fact takes the simple present in both clauses.)

answers.label: Q.16
answers.finalAnswer: (iii) should; (iii) might; (iii) need; (iii) ought to; (i) may
answers.solution:
(a) If the pain should return, take another of these pills. ('Should' after 'if' shows a possibility.)

(b) If you invited him he might come. (A past-tense 'if' clause takes would, might or could.)

(c) He need not hurry; there is plenty of time. (Absence of necessity.)

(d) One ought to serve one's country. ('Ought to' expresses a moral duty; 'should' and 'must' are also possible here.)

(e) We eat so that we may live. ('So that' expressing purpose takes 'may'.)

answers.solution:
I don't know what (a) Ø price (b) the owners are asking. But Kamal and Som are (c) the agents. You could give them (d) a ring and make them (e) an offer.

(a) 'What price' needs no article. (b) and (c): particular owners and particular agents of this property, so 'the'. (d) 'give someone a ring' is a fixed phrase. (e) 'offer' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an'.
